land.text: Mewar, held by the Guhilas to August 1303

predecessors.note: The Guhila dossier ends in August 1303 (Alauddin's capture of Chittor); Hammir Singh recovered Mewar from c. 1326. The infobox of the Mewar page begins at 566.

land.text: Udaipur State acceding to the Union of India

successors.note: The infobox says 1949; the body text says 1947.

capitals.name: Chittor (Chittorgarh)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Chittor (1213-1567)'; Chittor was Delhi's from 1303 until Hammir's recovery (undated).

capitals.name: Udaipur
capitals.note: Infobox 'Udaipur (1568-1585 and 1620-1949)'; under Mughal control in 1576-1585.

rulers.name: Hammir Singh
rulers.note: Reign years as printed in the table of the List of ranas of Mewar page (a titular Bhupal Singh 1948-1955 follows and is left off). The Kingdom of Mewar page's text differs by a year or two in places (Sanga's accession 1508 in the infobox, 1509 in the text, coronation 24 May 1509; Amar Singh II's death 1709 in the text against 1710 here).

minus.text: Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar

correction.text: the hill base of Hammir Singh: Mewar without Chittor and its eastern belt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (this dossier continues the sa-03 dossier of the Guhilas of Mewar, which ends in August 1303 with the Delhi capture of Chittor). 'c. 1326: Hammir Singh began regaining Mewar'; 'attempted to regain control of Mewar, but his initial efforts were thwarted'; 'established a base in Kelwara' after he 'seized the fort of Jilwara'; 'Maldev Songara from the Chauhan clan took charge of Mewar, successfully repelling Hammir's assaults'. Chittorgarh is left out until Singoli: 'Hammir later recaptured Chittorgarh and defeated the Delhi Sultanate forces at the Battle of Singoli' (no year; 1336 on the Muhammad bin Tughluq page). The hill country less a 60 km circle round Chittor is my reading, at confidence 1. [Repair 2026-10-20: the first keyframe ran 1326-1432 with the whole of Mewar, which the tughlaq-dynasty ledger still held until 1336 (its /ledger/15).]

correction.text: Mewar round Chittor and Udaipur, free of Delhi after Singoli (1336)

keyframe_review.note: 'Rana Hammir Singh liberated the strategic Rajputana following the victory in Battle of Singoli in 1336' (Muhammad bin Tughluq page); the Mewar page has Hammir recapturing Chittorgarh (no year). The infobox area, 33,030 km2 (1901), agrees with the gazetteer's Mewar region (about 33,400 km2).

correction.text: Mewar with Ajmer and Mandalgarh, 'inherited' by Kumbha in 1433

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'When Kumbha ascended the throne he had inherited whole of Mewar which consisted of' Chittorgarh, Kumbhalmer, Rajsamand, Mandalgarh, Ajmer, Mandsaur, Idar, Badnore, Jalore, Hadoti, Dungarpur and Banswara (Rana Kumbha page). Only Ajmer and Mandalgarh are drawn beyond the Mewar region; the gain event of 1433 records them at confidence 1.

union.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur (the Mandore circle of the kingdom-of-marwar dossier, short of Pali)

correction.text: Mewar with Ajmer and Mandalgarh and the Mandore country taken after Ranmal's death in 1438

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ranmal of Marwar was killed in 1438 (Marwar page: 'Rana Kumbha, son of Mokal, got him assassinated in 1438'); Mandore stayed away from Jodha until 1453 and the Rana Kumbha page has Jodha capturing 'his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar' in that year. The Marwar page does not say that Mewar occupied Mandore; the holder is the Rana Kumbha page's. [Repair 2026-10-20: new keyframe, with the matching loss in kingdom-of-marwar.]

correction.text: Mewar with Ajmer and Mandalgarh, Mandore returned to Marwar

keyframe_review.note: Mandore is back with Marwar in 1453 ('In 1453 AD, he was able to capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar'); Ajmer and Mandalgarh remain to Kumbha's side until the Malwa attacks of 1456-1457.

correction.text: without Mandalgarh and Ajmer, captured by Mahmud Khalji of Malwa in 1457

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'he successfully captured the fort [Mandalgarh] in October 1457', followed on the Mahmud Khalji page by 'Sultan Mahmud Khalji invaded and captured the fort of Ajmer' (no year); the Rana Kumbha page: 'Sultan of Malwa took Mewar territories up to Ajmer'. [Repair 2026-10-20: Ajmer is dropped here (it stayed in this shape to 1567 before): Maldeo took it in 1534 from Biram Dev of Merta, who 'had recently won Ajmer from the Gujarat Sultanate' (Maldeo Rathore page), so Mewar did not hold it then; kingdom-of-marwar also drew Ajmer in 1534-1543.]

correction.text: Mewar plus Ranthambore, Abu and Sirohi, conquered under Kumbha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, bridged to the end of Kumbha's reign (1468): 'Rana captured the areas of Gagron, Ranthambore, Sarangpur, and Narwar from the Malwa Sultanate'; 'He also conquered regions of Abu and Sirohi' (no years). The Kingdom of Mewar page instead has Kumbha 'reduced the rulers of Sirohi to vassals alongside Dungarpur'; drawn as land. Sarangpur and Narwar lie in the heart of Malwa and are not drawn. [Repair 2026-10-20: Gagron is dropped: malwa-sultanate holds it 1444-1530 with no loss, and the 1519 Battle of Gagron was fought against the Malwa Sultanate (Rana Sanga page). The keyframes of 1519 and 1528 are merged into this one: eastern Malwa is a contest, not Mewar land (see the 1519 events), and Chanderi was Medini Rai's, taken by Babur.]

minus.text: Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar

correction.text: Mewar without Chittor and the eastern belt, lost to the Mughals in 1567-1568

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Siege of Chittorgarh in 1567-1568 had led to the loss of the fertile eastern belt of Mewar to the Mughals.' Ranthambore, Abu and Sirohi are dropped here as a bridging judgment (no page opened says when Mewar lost them). The Mughal hold on Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh from 1576 to 1585 is a hatched occupation in the ledger.

correction.text: Mewar as returned by the treaty of 1615, to the accession to India

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Chittor and other Mughal occupied areas of Mewar would be returned to the Rana'; the infobox area of 33,030 km2 (1901) and 33,517 km2 (1941) matches this shape. Mandalgarh 'continued to remain under the Mughals'.

minus.text: Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar

region.text: the hill base of Hammir Singh at Kelwara and round it (Chittor still Delhi's)

ledger.note: c. 1326: Hammir Singh begins regaining Mewar. 'c. 1326: Hammir Singh began regaining Mewar'; 'attempted to regain control of Mewar, but his initial efforts were thwarted'; 'established a base in Kelwara' after he 'seized the fort of Jilwara'; infobox 'Maharana Hammir Singh: 1326-1364'. The Guhila line had ended with the fall of Chittor to Alauddin Khalji in 1303. The page names no earlier holder of the hill base, so the counterpart is 'nobody'; the struggle with Delhi is the contest below, and the whole of Mewar passes from Delhi in 1336. [Repair 2026-10-20: counterpart was tughlaq-dynasty, whose ledger (/ledger/15) loses Mewar in 1336, ten years later.]

region.text: Mewar, contested between Hammir Singh and Delhi's governors

ledger.note: 1326: Hammir Singh's war for Mewar begins. 'attempted to regain control of Mewar, but his initial efforts were thwarted'; 'Maldev Songara ... took charge of Mewar, successfully repelling Hammir's assaults' (Delhi's side). The first campaign that holds ground is the seizure of Jilwara and the base at Kelwara (undated on the page; 1326 is the page's year for the attempt).

region.text: Mewar, the field of the Singoli victory

ledger.note: 1336: the Battle of Singoli ends the contest. 'Rana Hammir Singh liberated the strategic Rajputana following the victory in Battle of Singoli in 1336' (Muhammad bin Tughluq page); the Kingdom of Mewar page has 'Hammir later recaptured Chittorgarh and defeated the Delhi Sultanate forces at the Battle of Singoli' (no year).

region.text: Mewar with Chittorgarh, freed from Delhi after Singoli

ledger.note: 1336: Delhi loses Mewar. The year and the victory are the page's ('liberated the strategic Rajputana following the victory in Battle of Singoli in 1336'); 'Rajputana' is the page's word, Mewar my reading, as in the tughlaq-dynasty ledger (/ledger/15, the matching loss). [Repair 2026-10-20: new event, agreeing the year with the Tughlaq dossier.]

region.text: Ajmer and Mandalgarh, held at Kumbha's accession

ledger.note: 1433: Ajmer and Mandalgarh are Mewar's when Kumbha takes the throne. 'When Kumbha ascended the throne he had inherited whole of Mewar which consisted of' Chittorgarh, Kumbhalmer, Rajsamand, Mandalgarh, Ajmer, Mandsaur, Idar, Badnore, Jalore, Hadoti, Dungarpur and Banswara (infobox reign 1433-1468). The page does not say when or from whom Mewar took Ajmer and Mandalgarh: a first-seen gain at confidence 1, counterpart 'nobody' (page silent). Idar, Jalore, Hadoti, Dungarpur, Banswara and Mandsaur are not drawn. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event; keyframe 1433 had Ajmer and Mandalgarh with no event.]

region.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur (the Mandore circle of the kingdom-of-marwar dossier, short of Pali)

ledger.note: 1438: Mewar holds Mandore. 'Rana Kumbha, son of Mokal, got him [Ranmal] assassinated in 1438' (Marwar page), and Jodha 'escaped Mewar'; the Rana Kumbha page has Jodha in 1453 'able to capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar', so Mewar held it in between. The Marwar page does not say that Mewar occupied Mandore (its infobox calls Marwar a 'vassal state of the Kingdom of Mewar (1428-1458; 1508-1527)'); 1438, Ranmal's death, is a bridging year. Mirrors the loss in kingdom-of-marwar.

region.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur (the Mandore circle of the kingdom-of-marwar dossier, short of Pali)

ledger.note: 1453: Jodha retakes Mandore. 'In 1453 AD, he was able to capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar' (Rana Kumbha page); the Marwar page: 'by 1453, he was able to regain Mandore'. Mirrors the regain in kingdom-of-marwar.

region.text: the fort of Ajmer

ledger.note: 1457 (bridging): Malwa takes Ajmer. 'Sultan Mahmud Khalji invaded and captured the fort of Ajmer' (Mahmud Khalji page; no year, listed after the capture of Mandalgarh in October 1457, inside his wars with Kumbha of 1442-1457); the Rana Kumbha page: 'Sultan of Malwa took Mewar territories up to Ajmer' (undated). Mirrored as a gain in malwa-sultanate. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event; the dossier drew Ajmer as Mewar's to 1567 although Maldeo took it from Biram Dev of Merta in 1534 (Maldeo Rathore page).]

region.text: the fort of Mandalgarh

ledger.note: 1457: Mahmud Khalji takes Mandalgarh. 'he successfully captured the fort in October 1457' after an earlier attack failed (Malwa's wars with Rana Kumbha, 1442-1446 and after).

region.text: Ranthambore

ledger.note: 1468: Kumbha's conquest of Ranthambore, bridged to the end of his reign. 'Rana captured the areas of Gagron, Ranthambore, Sarangpur, and Narwar from the Malwa Sultanate' and 'conquered regions of Abu and Sirohi' (Rana Kumbha page; no years). Ranthambore is not in the malwa-sultanate shape and no page opened has Malwa holding it, so the counterpart is the place, not malwa-sultanate. Gagron, Sarangpur and Narwar are not drawn. [Repair 2026-10-20: Gagron dropped from the event: malwa-sultanate holds it from February 1444 (Mahmud Khalji page) to 1530 with no loss, and the 1519 Battle of Gagron was fought against the Malwa Sultanate (Rana Sanga page), so it cannot have been Mewar's in 1519; the confidence-1 gain of 1468 stays only for Ranthambore.]

region.text: Abu and Sirohi

ledger.note: 1468: Kumbha takes Abu and Sirohi (undated on the page; bridged to the end of his reign). The Kingdom of Mewar page has Kumbha instead 'reduced the rulers of Sirohi to vassals alongside Dungarpur, which was in rebellion' (read again 2026-10-20); the circle is drawn as land and overlaps the Jalore circle of kingdom-of-marwar (1538-1563) at the frontier.

region.text: eastern Malwa, Medini Rai's Chanderi

ledger.note: 1519: Sanga overruns eastern Malwa. 'After the 1519 Battle of Gagron against the Malwa Sultanate, he captured much of eastern Malwa'; 'Sanga captured eastern and northern Malwa and Chanderi' (1518-1519 per Satish Chandra, as the page quotes him); Medini Rai, 'a rebellious minister of the Malwa sultan', was his vassal, and 'Silhaditya Tomar established himself as ruler of Raisen and the Sarangpur region'. The Malwa Sultanate page: 'much of the Sultanate came under the brief control of Maharana of Mewar Rana Sanga'. [Repair 2026-10-20: this contest is now the only model of the episode, shared with malwa-sultanate (its /ledger 10-11). The earlier 'gain' of the same circle (and the 1528 'loss' of it to the Mughals) are dropped: malwa-sultanate records only a contest, so 46,000 km2 was drawn by both states in 1519-1527.] Chanderi itself (Medini Rai's seat, 78.13 E 24.72 N) lies outside the 100 km circle round Bhopal; the circle is kept because Chanderi is not in the gazetteer.

region.text: Idar and northern Gujarat

ledger.note: 1520: Sanga invades Gujarat over Idar. 'In 1520, Sanga invaded Gujarat because of the succession of the state of Idar with an army of 40,000 Rajputs' ('Rai Mal, assisted by Rana Sanga, defeated Muzzafar Shah II in 1517'); the Gujarat Sultanate page has Sanga annexing northern Gujarat after the 1519 battle.

region.text: eastern Malwa

ledger.note: 1528: Sanga dies and the contest closes. Sanga died 'in Kalpi in January 1528 or on 20 May' (infobox 30 January 1528); 'Babur captured Chanderi, earlier ruled by Rai, after his victory' (Rana Sanga page: Babur's victory at Khanwa, no year for Chanderi); 'Silhadi' of Raisen changed sides at Khanwa. The Medini Rai page gives his service as 1511-1528. The end of the Malwa contest is a bridging year; the land stays in the malwa-sultanate shape (to 1530). [Repair 2026-10-20: the loss of this circle to mughal-empire (confidence 2) is dropped: Babur took only Chanderi, outside the circle, and the Raisen and Sarangpur country stayed with Silhaditya Tomar (a name; gujarat-sultanate /ledger/19 gains Raisen from 'Raisen' in 1531).]

region.text: Idar and northern Gujarat

ledger.note: 1532: the Idar contest closes in the sources' silence. The Mewar page does not say how the Idar dispute ended; Bahadur Shah of Gujarat first besieged Chittor in 1532 ('a 1533 siege had ended with a ransom payment' on this page), and by 1535 the Gujarat pages show all Gujarat under its sultan.

region.text: Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar

ledger.note: 1567: Akbar besieges Chittor. 'The Siege of Chittorgarh in 1567-1568 had led to the loss of the fertile eastern belt of Mewar to the Mughals.'

region.text: Chittor

ledger.note: 1568: Chittor falls. 'The Siege of Chittorgarh in 1567-1568 had led to the loss of the fertile eastern belt of Mewar to the Mughals'; 'damage inflicted by Mughal forces in 1568 to Chittor' (Mewar page).

region.text: the fertile eastern belt of Mewar with Chittor

ledger.note: 1568: the Mughals take Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar.

region.text: Kumbha's outer conquests

ledger.note: 1568: Ranthambore, Abu and Sirohi are no longer Mewar's. No page opened dates their loss; the Mewar of 1585 and of 1901 is the core only, so they are dropped here (bridging). [Repair 2026-10-20: Ajmer and Gagron are out of the event: Ajmer went to Malwa in 1457 and Gagron was never Mewar's.]
1568: the capital is Udaipur. Infobox 'Chittor (1213-1567)', 'Udaipur (1568-1585 and 1620-1949)'.

region.text: Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh

ledger.note: 1576: the Mughals hold Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh. After Haldighati (18 June 1576) 'Akbar led a campaign in September 1576, and Gogunda, Udaipur, and Kumbhalgarh were all under Mughal control'; Pratap withdrew to the hills.

region.text: Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh

ledger.note: 1585: Pratap recovers much of Mewar. 'From 1585 till his death, the Rana had recovered a large part of Mewar', though he 'could not fulfill his dream of capturing Chittor itself'; Mughal pressure eased after 1579.
1585: the court is at Chawand. Infobox 'Chawand (1585-1620)'; the Maharana Pratap page describes his court at Chavand, where he died on 19 January 1597.

region.text: Chittor and the Mughal-occupied lands of Mewar

ledger.note: 1615: the treaty returns Chittor. 'In February 1615, Khurram and Amar Singh met' (Mewar page); 'Chittor and other Mughal occupied areas of Mewar would be returned to the Rana', but 'the Chittor fort would never be repaired'; the page gives no year for the actual return ('given back as a goodwill gesture').

region.text: Mewar as a Mughal tributary after the treaty of 1615

ledger.note: February 1615: Mewar accepts a Mughal overlord. 'In February 1615, Khurram and Amar Singh met in Gogundah'; the terms: 'Maharana's eldest son would serve under the Emperor', 'Maharana would provide a 1000 horsemen contingent in the Mughal Army', 'Maharana would never try to return to Chittorgarh'; Mewar 'later ... became a tributary state with a significant degree of autonomy' (Kingdom of Mewar page; the word 'vassal' is not used, and the status is undated beyond the treaty). Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord); the mughal-empire owner should carry the mirror entry. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event; the dossier drew Mewar sovereign from 1615 to 1949.]
1620: the capital is Udaipur again. Infobox 'Udaipur (1568-1585 and 1620-1949)'; the Amar Singh page says 'Udaipur remained the capital of Mewar State' (a disagreement).

region.text: Mewar, no longer a Mughal tributary

ledger.note: 1707 (bridging): the Mughal tie lapses. The page dates no end: 'In 1707, Aurangzeb died and his sons started the war of succession' and Amar Singh II 'captured the granted cities that were under Mughal control'; 'Starting from 1711 ... the Marathas started raiding into the Rajputana'; Sangram Singh II 'was allowed to mint his own coins in 1713' by Farrukhsiyar; Peshwa Baji Rao secured chauth in February 1736; the introduction speaks of 'de facto independence for Mewar' (no year). 1707 is a bridging year at confidence 1; the end could as well be 1713 or 1736.

region.text: Mewar under the East India Company's supremacy

ledger.note: 13 January 1818: Mewar accepts British supremacy. 'The Treaty of Friendship, Alliances and Unity was concluded between Mewar and EIC on 13 January 1818'; 'Mewar acknowledged British supremacy' and agreed 'to pay one-fourth of its revenues as tribute for 5 years, and three-eight in perpetuity'; the introduction: 'accepting British suzerainty in 1818'. The page does not use 'protectorate' or 'subsidiary'. Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord); 'british-empire' is the Cliopatria row of 1757-1858, and the owner of the East India Company or the Raj should carry the mirror entry. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event.]

region.text: Mewar (Udaipur State) until it joined the Union of India

ledger.note: 1947: British supremacy ends. 'remained a princely state until it joined the Union of India in 1947'; 'A constitution for Udaipur State was adopted on 23 May 1947' (the infobox has 'Accession to the Union of India: 1949'). The state itself ends in 1949 (dissolve).

region.text: Mewar (Udaipur State)

ledger.note: 1949: Mewar accedes to the Union of India. Infobox 'Accession to the Union of India: 1949' (the body text says 'joined the Union of India in 1947'; a constitution for Udaipur State was adopted on 23 May 1947).

wars.name: Hammir Singh's war for Mewar
wars.outcome: Hammir took a base at Kelwara and, after the victory at Singoli in 1336, freed Mewar from Delhi.
wars.note: 'Rana Hammir Singh liberated the strategic Rajputana following the victory in Battle of Singoli in 1336' (Muhammad bin Tughluq page); the Mewar page gives no years but 1326.

wars.name: Malwa-Mewar wars
wars.outcome: Kumbha's forces took Sultan Mahmud of Malwa prisoner in 1437; Mahmud Khalji captured Mandalgarh in October 1457.

wars.name: Mewar and Marwar over Mandore

zones.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur (the Mandore circle of the kingdom-of-marwar dossier, short of Pali)

wars.outcome: Ranmal of Marwar was killed in 1438 by Kumbha's party; Mandore passed to Mewar until Jodha retook it in 1453.
wars.note: Marwar page: 'Rana Kumbha, son of Mokal, got him assassinated in 1438'; 'by 1453, he was able to regain Mandore'. The Marwar page does not say that Mewar held Mandore; the Rana Kumbha page does.

wars.name: Gujarat-Malwa attack on Kumbhalgarh
wars.outcome: 'In S. 1513 (A.D. 1456) the Sultan of Gujrat "despairing of reducing Chitor" arrived near Abu'; Kumbha 'defeated Imad-ul-Mulk with great slaughter'; no land changed.

wars.name: Sanga's wars with the Lodis
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Lodi 'marched against Mewar in 1517' and was beaten at Khatoli, again in 1518-19 at Dholpur; no land is dated.

wars.name: Battle of Gagron
wars.outcome: Sanga defeated Mahmud Khilji II and 'captured much of eastern Malwa'.

wars.name: Battle of Bayana and Khanwa
wars.outcome: 'In the February 1527 Battle of Bayana, he defeated Babur's Mughal forces'; at Khanwa on 16 March 'the Mughals were victorious' (year inferred by the page's timeline).

wars.name: Gujarat's sieges of Chittor
wars.outcome: A siege of 1533 ended with a ransom; Bahadur Shah sacked Chittor in 1535. The pages do not show a change of owner.

wars.name: Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-1568)
wars.outcome: Akbar took Chittor and the eastern belt of Mewar.

wars.name: Battle of Haldighati and the Mughal occupation
wars.outcome: Haldighati (18 June 1576) was indecisive; Gogunda, Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh were under Mughal control from September 1576; Pratap recovered a large part of Mewar from 1585.

wars.name: Mughal-Mewar war under Amar Singh I
wars.outcome: Jahangir's armies (1606, 1608, 1609-1611) failed; Prince Khurram's campaign of 1613-1615 ended in the treaty of February 1615, which returned Chittor and the occupied lands.

certainty.note: No survey line is on the pages opened; Mewar's frontiers with the Rajput neighbours and the hills are approximate. The treaty of 13 January 1818 with the East India Company names no boundary.

notes:
No Cliopatria row after the Guhilas (the sa-03 dossier guhilas-of-mewar names this slug as successor). Six pages (Kingdom of Mewar, Rana Kumbha, Rana Sanga, Maharana Pratap, Amar Singh I, plus Mahmud Khalji already read for Malwa). The pages give few years: Kumbha's conquests, the Bahadur Shah siege of 1533, the Haldighati occupation's end and the return of Chittor after 1615 are undated; the body text of the Mewar page gives 14,000 km2 for 1941 against its infobox's 33,517 km2; the gazetteer's Mewar region (33,383 km2) matches the infobox.
The sa-05-x batch (Rajput states from 1526) may also carry this state: check polities/ before editing.
Disagreements: Sanga's accession 1508 (infobox) or 1509 (text, coronation 24 May 1509); his death 30 January 1528, January 1528 at Kalpi or 20 May; Gagron 1518 or 1519 on the same page; Udaipur as capital 1568-1585 and 1620-1949 (infobox) against 'Udaipur remained the capital' (Amar Singh page); accession to India 1947 (text) or 1949 (infobox).
Not settled: when Hammir recovered Chittor; Kumbha's conquests (Gagron, Ranthambore, Sarangpur, Narwar, Abu, Sirohi, Hadoti, Nagaur, Bundi: no years) and their loss (bridged to 1568, confidence 1); Mewar's status as a Mughal vassal after 1615 and a British protectorate from 13 January 1818 (the vassal events belong to mughal-empire and british-empire; Dungarpur and Banswara 'would again become vassals of Mewar' in 1615, no end); Maratha raids 1761-1773 (no land); Udai Singh II's reign and the founding of Udaipur (1557 Haramada, not dated for Udaipur); the Mewar-Gujarat Idar dispute's end (1532 is a bridging year); no ruler strip (the infobox lists seven reigns only).
